items.title: Edward "Eddie" Richardson Interview, 1960-10-29
items.q: Let's see, when you first came into the Eureka, who was playing tuba? Clok. This man they called Clok.

ctx.x: Yeah, that's an old march Maryland. What about songs coming back in those days? What would you play coming back? For the second line? Oh like from a funeral? Mm-hmm. Well they played like the Sheik, Maury, put on your old gray bonnet. Yeah, those three numbers, I'd about hold them up. Old gray bonnet used to be a hit one time. When did the band start playing blues? Well those blues was mostly used in like dance halls. And when they'd get around about 10 o'clock, 11 o'clock, they'd start playing blues. They'd have…

Well, what happened after you left René? Well, that's when I tried to organize my own band. I didn't have any luck. Oh, I see. So, uh, let me see now. Then after that, who did you join up with? Well, it was quite a while. They had a man by the name of Jimmy Jackson. Jackson had a band. And he got in touch with me whenever he'd get parade jobs, well he'd hire me, play with them. Jackson's band, Jimmy Jackson's band. And what did he play? He didn't play anything at all. He was mostly a music director. He'd walk in…
out. Were they still having any lawn parties?
